TYLCV shows upward-curling, cupped leaves with interveinal yellowing — doesn't match. Septoria shows scattered small circular spots — doesn't match.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: green tomato leaf with **brown necrotic margins extending inward in a wedge/V-shape**, interveinal yellowing, no discrete spots, no powdery/mold coating
- Verticillium_Wilt reference: exact match — brown necrotic margins with V-shaped inward progression, interveinal yellowing, one-sided symptom expression
- All other candidates ruled out: Late_Blight (oily blotches), Leaf_Mold (pale/whitish with underside mold), TYLCV (leaf curling/cupping), Septoria (small circular spots), Early_Blight (concentric ring target spots)
